title: edgeburst latency bifurcation dashboard (model+route, streaming vs non-streaming)
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Problem: Product and SRE teams need a single interactive surface that highlights how latency behaves across model families and API routes with an explicit split between streaming and non-streaming I/O modes. Existing dashboards show percentiles by route or by model, but they do not make the streaming vs non-streaming bifurcation first-class, and they lack trace-level drilldowns for long-tail events. This ticket scopes the design and implementation of a new 'Edgeburst' dashboard that provides p50/p95/p99 views, cohort slices by request shape, and direct trace links for tail latencies.

Why now: Recent customer incidents and postmortems called out regressed p99s on a streaming fallback path. We need faster root-cause (model vs route vs serving path) identification and an observable that can be used for runbooks and automated SLO alerts.

Out-of-scope: any changes to tokenization or core model kernels. Does not include rollout of new autoscaling policies — those are being tracked in ENG-772300.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard contains panels for p50/p95/p99 latency split by (model_family, route) and I/O mode (streaming vs non-streaming)
Each panel supports cohorting (prompt_length buckets: short/medium/long) and concurrency buckets (1-4, 5-20, 21+)
Panels include direct trace links (trace_id) that open the Trace Viewer filtered to the event
Tracing hooks capture servepath stage durations (parse -> route -> compile -> kv-cache -> token-gen) and are present for >= 95% of sampled requests
New metrics emitted do not increase P95 write latency for our metrics pipeline by more than 5% (verified in staging)
SLO alert rules for p95 and p99 regressions are defined and wired into the runbook with playbook links
Dashboard documented in Console Observability runbook and demo shown to SRE/PM/UX reviewers
implementation_plan:
1) Instrumentation: add structured timing tags to tracing hooks for servepath stages and ensure tags for model.family and route.name are attached.
2) Metrics pipeline: add a streaming-aware label io_mode={streaming,nonstreaming} to latency histograms in metrics exporter. Update logs to include a lightweight latency JSON envelope for fallback detection.
3) Ingest: update metrics ingestion mapping (metrics bridge) to forward io_mode label and percentile-ready histograms.
4) Queries: author percentile queries and pre-aggregated rollups for high-cardinality model+route combinations.
5) Dashboard: create panels, cohort selectors, and trace link actions.
6) Validation: run a canary with synthetic traffic (short/medium/long shapes) and compare to baseline dashboards.
7) Rollout: staging -> dedicated -> hosted with feature flag 'edgeburst-latency-v1' and communicate to customers via internal changelog.
telemetry_queries: PromQL example: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(serve_latency_ms_bucket{io_mode=~"streaming|nonstreaming"}[5m])) by (le, model_family, route_name, io_mode))

ClickHouse example: SELECT quantileExact(0.99)(latency_ms) AS p99, model_family, route_name, io_mode FROM metrics_latency WHERE timestamp >= now() - INTERVAL 1 HOUR GROUP BY model_family, route_name, io_mode
Log pipeline enrichment: add field 'io_mode' at exporter step using request.metadata.io_mode (fallback detection sets nonstreaming when stream closed)
dashboard_panels: Model x Route latency matrix (heatmap) with p50/p95/p99 toggles and io_mode filter
Servepath waterfall for selected cell showing stage durations and KV cache hit rate
Streaming vs Non-streaming percentile overlay time-series (selectable model_family or route)
Cohort slicer: prompt length and concurrency selector with p95 delta bar chart
Top-50 traces for selected cell (links to Trace Viewer) with quick tags for error_class and fallback_reason
SLO trendboard: daily p95 and p99 with annotation for deploys and capacity events
Alert panel listing active SLO violations and playbook links
